items.name: B2B SaaS
items.pattern: Hero with one clear promise + logo wall + 3 feature blocks + pricing + FAQ + CTA
items.colorMood: Trust blue carries the page; one warm accent is reserved for the CTA and nothing else
items.typeMood: Professional, strong hierarchy, nothing decorative
effects: sticky header that shrinks on scroll

decisionRules.then: drop glassmorphism on tables — translucency destroys legibility at density; keep it for the marketing hero only
waitlist pattern — one CTA, no pricing table, and no fabricated testimonials or logo wall
surface SOC2/SSO/audit-log signals above the fold; a procurement lead scans for those before features
the CTA is 'Start free' and reaches a working product in one click — no demo-request wall

antiPatterns: Dark mode by default — B2B buyers scan in bright offices
Stock-photo hero of people pointing at a laptop
A testimonial carousel that auto-advances past the one being read
Pricing hidden behind 'Contact us' for a self-serve product

pages.dashboard: Sidebar nav + a KPI row + one primary table. Density over whitespace — this is a tool, not a brochure.

items.name: Micro SaaS / Indie product
items.pattern: Hero + a real screenshot or demo GIF above the fold + one price + a founder note
items.colorMood: Friendly and distinct — a small product wins on personality, not on looking like an enterprise
items.typeMood: Warm, direct, human — write like a person, not a committee
effects: an inline demo that runs without signup

decisionRules.then: put it above the fold and let people use it before signing up — for an unknown indie product, trust is the whole conversion problem
say so with a face and a name; being small is the differentiator, not something to hide behind corporate voice
show a single card, not a three-tier table that fakes a lineup you don't have

antiPatterns: Pretending to be a big company (fake 'Team' page, invented logo wall)
A three-tier pricing table for one product
Enterprise voice on an indie product — it reads as a lie

items.name: Fintech / Banking
items.pattern: Hero with the trust signal + how it works in 3 steps + security section + regulatory footer + CTA
items.colorMood: Money being counted carefully — deep green over graphite, never playful
items.typeMood: Authoritative and precise; tabular numerals everywhere a figure appears
effects: numbers that count up once on reveal, never on loop

decisionRules.then: the disclosure is body text near the claim — never behind a tooltip, an accordion, or 6pt grey. That placement is a legal question, not a layout preference
tabular numerals + explicit currency + never rely on red/green alone for +/- — colour-blind users read the sign, not the hue
a confirm step that restates amount and recipient in full; no one-tap transfers
lead with what it costs; a hidden fee discovered later costs more trust than the fee itself

antiPatterns: Playful illustration next to someone's actual balance
Green/red as the only signal for gain/loss
Fine print as the accessibility strategy
Fake urgency on a financial decision

items.name: Crypto / Web3
items.pattern: Hero + live protocol stats + how it works + audit/security proof + connect-wallet CTA
items.colorMood: Bullion on carbon — gold against near-black with one electric accent
items.typeMood: Technical and confident; mono for every address and hash

decisionRules.then: show the destination address in full at confirm, in mono, with a copy button — truncation is where people lose funds
state the risk and the timeframe with equal weight; a number with no downside next to it is marketing, not information
explain what will be signed before the wallet modal opens; a blind signature request is how drainers work
link the actual audit report, not a badge — a badge nobody can click is decoration

antiPatterns: Truncated addresses at the confirm step
APY with no risk statement
Countdown urgency on an investment decision
Neon glow at such low contrast that the numbers are unreadable

items.name: Healthcare / Telemedicine
items.pattern: Hero with the reassurance + find-care flow + credentials + insurance/cost clarity + book CTA
items.colorMood: Competent care, not emergency — teal and cool white that calms rather than alarms
items.typeMood: Plainly readable at a glance; assume the reader is anxious, tired, or on a phone in a waiting room
effects: clear step indicators on any flow

decisionRules.if: the reader may be anxious or in pain
decisionRules.then: shorten every path and remove every optional field — cognitive load is a symptom here, not a metric
state it plainly and early; surprise medical billing is the category's defining harm
no third-party analytics on pages carrying health data, and never put a condition in a URL — that leaks to referrers and logs
a persistent, unmissable route to emergency care that never sits behind a menu
16px floor is not enough — start at 18px and test at 200% zoom

antiPatterns: Red as a primary — it reads as emergency to a worried patient
Playful illustration next to a diagnosis
A condition name in the URL
Dark patterns on appointment cancellation

items.name: E-commerce / Retail
items.pattern: Hero or category grid + product grid with real photography + PDP + cart + a short checkout
items.colorMood: Warm retail urgency — burnt orange that makes Buy feel like the obvious next move
items.typeMood: Clean and out of the way; the product photo is the design
effects: cart drawer instead of a page jump

decisionRules.if: shipping cost or delivery date is knowable
decisionRules.then: show it on the product page — surprise shipping at checkout is the single biggest cart-abandonment cause in the category
offer it first; a forced account is a conversion tax you pay on every order
show availability per variant before selection, not after — nothing is worse than picking a size to learn it's gone
fix the photography before the layout; no amount of CSS rescues bad product images in this category

antiPatterns: Shipping cost revealed only at the last checkout step
Forced account creation before purchase
A hero carousel nobody clicks past slide one
Fake countdown timers that reset on refresh

pages.checkout: One column, a visible step indicator, no nav to escape through, and the order total pinned in view at every step.

items.name: Luxury / Fashion
items.pattern: Full-bleed editorial imagery + minimal nav + lookbook + a deliberately quiet product grid
items.colorMood: Near-black, bone white, one champagne accent — restraint is the signal of expense
items.typeMood: High-contrast display serif with enormous whitespace; the type is the luxury
effects: slow deliberate fades (400ms is allowed here, and only here)
hover that reveals rather than shouts

decisionRules.then: remove, don't add — badges, urgency and discount language destroy the positioning faster than any layout flaw
budget the LCP for it: AVIF, preload the hero, and never lazy-load the first image
show it plainly — hiding price reads as evasive, not exclusive

antiPatterns: Sale badges and countdowns on a luxury brand
Cramped grids — whitespace IS the product here
Stock photography of any kind
Slow, unoptimized hero images (the aesthetic dies at 6s LCP)

items.name: Restaurant / Food
items.pattern: Hero food photography + the menu + hours & location + a reservation or order CTA
items.colorMood: Appetite on a cream tablecloth — warm reds and olive, never cold blue
items.typeMood: Characterful and warm; a little personality is the point

decisionRules.then: hours, address, phone and menu are the whole site — put them one tap away. Nobody browses a restaurant site; they are standing outside, hungry
make it real HTML — a PDF menu is unreadable on a phone and invisible to search, and this is the category's most common self-inflicted wound
link the platform directly; don't rebuild a checkout you can't staff

antiPatterns: A PDF menu
An autoplay video with sound
Hours buried in a footer
Cold blue palettes — they measurably suppress appetite

items.name: Beauty / Spa / Wellness
items.pattern: Calm hero + treatments list with prices + practitioner bios + booking flow
items.colorMood: Exhaling — dusty rose and sage on warm plaster; quiet and skin-adjacent
items.typeMood: Airy elegant serif with a light sans; generous line-height, nothing shouty

decisionRules.then: price and duration sit on the treatment itself — 'enquire for pricing' loses the booking to the salon that just said £45, 60 min
the interface must be calm: no urgency, no popups, no carousel. A stressful booking flow contradicts the entire product
real faces and real names — this is a trust-with-my-body purchase

antiPatterns: Exit-intent popups on a relaxation brand
'Enquire for pricing' on standard treatments
Saturated high-energy colour
Stock photos of orchids and hot stones

items.name: Fitness / Gym
items.pattern: High-energy hero + programmes + transformation proof + pricing + join CTA
items.colorMood: The last rep — volt screaming off charcoal
items.typeMood: Heavy condensed display, all-caps allowed, high energy

decisionRules.then: huge touch targets and high contrast — sweaty hands, a phone on the floor, and glare are the real design constraints
real members with consent; stock 'before/after' is both obvious and legally risky
state the contract length and cancellation terms up front — the category's reputation problem is entirely about the exit

antiPatterns: Tiny controls used with sweaty hands
Hidden contract terms
Body-shaming copy
Motion so aggressive it triggers reduced-motion users

items.name: Education / LMS
items.pattern: Hero with the outcome + curriculum + instructor credibility + outcomes/reviews + enrol CTA
items.colorMood: Approachable scholarship — indigo with a highlighter amber for progress
items.typeMood: Readable for long stretches; this is a reading product

decisionRules.then: long-form readability wins over brand expression — line length ≤75ch, 1.6 line-height, and a genuinely usable dark mode for late nights
make it visible and honest; a fake progress bar is the fastest way to lose a learner's trust
the ux-research brief is about the teacher and parent too — they choose, the child uses
publish real completion and outcome numbers, or don't claim an outcome

antiPatterns: Gamification that distracts from the learning
Autoplay video on module open
Endless scroll with no sense of position in the course
Certificates presented as accreditation when they aren't

items.name: Kids / Family
items.pattern: Big playful hero + what it does, for the parent + safety & privacy + the child-facing experience
items.colorMood: Primary-colour joy with the volume up
items.typeMood: Rounded, friendly, large — and readable by an emerging reader

decisionRules.then: targets at 64px+ and forgive every mis-tap — small motor control is the constraint, and an undo is worth more than a confirm dialog
there are two users with different jobs: the parent's page sells safety and value, the child's screen is the product. Never mix them
COPPA/GDPR-K applies — say plainly what is collected, and never put a purchase behind a child's tap
icons plus words, not icons alone; and read the copy aloud to check it

antiPatterns: In-app purchases reachable by a child's tap
Dark patterns aimed at children — indefensible, full stop
Tiny text for early readers
Data collection without a clear parental gate

items.name: Gaming
items.pattern: Cinematic hero (trailer) + screenshots + features + system requirements + wishlist/buy CTA
items.colorMood: A dark room lit by a screen — magenta and cyan burning on true black
items.typeMood: Technical, angular, energetic

decisionRules.then: it is the hero — but muted, with controls, and never autoplaying sound
system requirements are a real section, not a footnote; it is the question every buyer actually has
never pure #000 with pure #FFF text — the halation is genuinely painful over time. Use near-black and near-white

antiPatterns: Autoplay trailer with sound
Neon at 2:1 contrast — unreadable is not a style
Hiding the price behind a launcher
Motion that ignores prefers-reduced-motion

items.name: Streaming / Entertainment
items.pattern: Featured hero + content rails by category + a detail overlay + continue-watching
items.colorMood: Lights down, poster art up — signature red on cinema black
items.typeMood: Bold and out of the way; the artwork is the interface
effects: hover preview after a deliberate delay

decisionRules.then: they must be keyboard and screen-reader navigable — a horizontal rail is the single most commonly inaccessible pattern on the web
delay it ~700ms; instant preview makes a mouse crossing the grid fire a dozen videos
reserve the poster's aspect-ratio box before the image lands, or every rail shifts as it loads

antiPatterns: Rails that only work with a mouse
Autoplay with sound on page load
Titles rendered only as text baked into artwork
Layout shift as posters load in

items.name: Music / Audio
items.pattern: Artist/album hero + player + releases + tour dates + listen CTA
items.colorMood: Stage-light purple with a hot pink spill — nocturnal and loud
items.typeMood: Expressive display; this is a brand, not a form

decisionRules.then: it persists across navigation — audio that stops when someone clicks a link is the category's cardinal sin
gate it behind prefers-reduced-motion and pause it when the tab is hidden; it is a battery and vestibular hazard otherwise
they are the commercial page — put them above the fold with the city, not below a bio nobody reads

antiPatterns: Audio that stops on navigation
Autoplay music on load
A visualizer that ignores reduced-motion
Text baked into album-art images

items.name: News / Editorial
items.pattern: Lead story + a hierarchy of secondary stories + section nav + the article page as the real product
items.colorMood: Newsprint authority — black on paper with one red reserved for the thing that matters
items.typeMood: A real reading typeface at a real reading size; hierarchy by weight and scale, not colour
effects: almost none — motion is a distraction in a reading product

decisionRules.then: protect the reading column above everything: ≤75ch, 1.6 line-height, 18-20px. Every element that competes with the text is a bug
reserve their exact box up front — ad-driven layout shift is the #1 CLS cause on news sites and it drives readers away permanently
timestamp and update log are visible; 'when was this written' is the reader's first question
state the limit before the click, not after the reader is invested — and never cloak content from crawlers you show to readers

antiPatterns: An interstitial before the first paragraph
Ads that reflow the article mid-sentence
Infinite scroll that hijacks the back button
Undated articles

pages.article: One column, ≤75ch, no sidebar competing with the text. Byline, date, reading time. Related links AFTER the piece, never beside it.

items.name: Portfolio / Personal
items.pattern: A statement hero + selected work + one case study per project + contact
items.colorMood: Gallery walls — warm paper and ink, with one burnt-orange hyperlink
items.typeMood: Confident display type; the typography IS the portfolio

decisionRules.then: show the thinking, not just the final render — process is what gets someone hired; a grid of pretty screenshots is not a case study
fewer, deeper is stronger than more, shallower — three real case studies beat twelve thumbnails
make contact trivially findable; a portfolio that hides the email fails at its only job

antiPatterns: A grid of screenshots with no context
A clever intro animation between the visitor and the work
No contact route
Client work shown without permission

items.name: Agency / Studio
items.pattern: Bold statement hero + selected work + services + team + a real contact CTA
items.colorMood: Confident and slightly rude — near-black with an acid accent
items.typeMood: Oversized, opinionated display; the site is the portfolio piece

decisionRules.then: it must be flawless where it counts — an agency site with a 4s LCP or a failing contrast ratio has already answered the client's question
reduced-motion support is not optional here; it is a public demonstration of whether you know your craft
lead with the outcome, not the aesthetic — clients buy results

antiPatterns: A scroll-jacked homepage
A loader animation on a site with nothing to load
Case studies with no results
Style that fails the a11y basics — it is the loudest possible signal of unseriousness

items.name: Developer Tools
items.pattern: Hero with the install command + a code example that actually runs + docs link + GitHub
items.colorMood: Built for people who live in a terminal but ship a GUI — slate with a signal accent
items.typeMood: Mono for anything executable; a clean sans for prose
effects: syntax highlighting that matches the real theme

decisionRules.then: the install command goes above the fold with a copy button — this audience wants to try it, not read about it. Every scroll before the code costs you
a real, runnable example beats any feature list; a curl that works is the entire pitch
the GitHub link, the licence and the star count are trust signals — surface them
ship it properly; this audience overwhelmingly uses it and will judge you on the code block

antiPatterns: Marketing copy where the code example should be
A signup wall before the docs
Screenshots of code instead of copyable text
Syntax highlighting that doesn't match any real theme

pages.docs: Persistent sidebar, search that works, copyable code, and a version switcher. Density is correct here — this is a reference, not a story.

items.name: AI / ML Product
items.pattern: Hero with a live demo + how it works + accuracy/limits + pricing by usage + try CTA
items.colorMood: Iris violet into cyan — the current house style for intelligence, used with restraint
items.typeMood: Modern and clean; let the demo speak
effects: a demo that runs without signup

decisionRules.then: state its limits next to its claims — the category's trust problem is entirely overpromising, and an honest limits section converts better than a superlative
render tokens as they arrive with a stable container; a jumping layout during generation makes a fast model feel broken
say so in the interface, not in the terms — and make correction/regeneration one click
give a real cost example; 'per 1M tokens' means nothing to someone who has never counted tokens

antiPatterns: Purple gradient as the entire brand — it now reads as generic AI
Claims with no stated limits
A demo behind a signup wall
Fake typing animation on a cached response

items.name: Analytics Dashboard
items.pattern: Filter bar + KPI row + the primary chart + a supporting table + drill-down
items.colorMood: A wall of numbers that stays readable at 2am — deep blue-slate with signal accents
items.typeMood: Tabular numerals, tight and legible at small sizes
effects: skeletons sized to the real chart

decisionRules.if: someone stares at this for hours
decisionRules.then: density beats whitespace and a real dark mode is a health feature, not a preference — design for the 8-hour user, not the screenshot
never colour alone: pair it with shape, label or pattern. ~8% of men cannot distinguish your red and green series
reserve the chart's exact box — a dashboard that reflows as each panel lands is unusable on a slow connection
state the unit, the timezone and the comparison period on the tile, not in a tooltip

antiPatterns: Glassmorphism behind a data table
Chart junk — 3D pie charts, gradients on bars
Colour as the only series channel
A spinner where a skeleton belongs

pages.dashboard: Filters top, KPIs in a row, one hero chart, supporting table below. Everything above the fold answers 'is anything broken?' in under 5 seconds.

items.name: Productivity / Notes / Tasks
items.pattern: Hero showing the actual interface + the core loop + integrations + pricing
items.colorMood: A desk with nothing on it — warm graphite and paper, colour only where you must act
items.typeMood: Quiet and legible; the user's content is the design

decisionRules.then: keyboard-first: every primary action has a shortcut and a command palette. Daily users graduate to the keyboard or they leave

decisionRules.if: the user's content is the point
decisionRules.then: the chrome recedes — brand colour on every panel competes with the thing they came to write
optimistic and instantly reversible; a 300ms round-trip on a checkbox makes the product feel broken

antiPatterns: A loading spinner on a checkbox
Brand colour competing with user content
Onboarding that blocks the empty state instead of seeding it
No keyboard support in a daily-driver tool

items.name: Social / Community
items.pattern: Feed + composer + profile + notifications + a discovery surface
items.colorMood: Warm, social and a little hot — fuchsia with a tangerine like
items.typeMood: Compact and friendly; a lot of content per screen
effects: smooth infinite scroll with a stable scroll position

decisionRules.then: preserve scroll position on back — losing someone's place in a feed is the fastest way to lose the session
moderation, reporting and blocking are core UI, not settings buried three levels deep. Ship them with v1 or you are building a harassment vector
ask honestly whether it serves the user or the metric — this is the category where that question actually matters
reserve aspect-ratio boxes; a feed that jumps as images load is the worst CLS experience on the web

antiPatterns: Losing scroll position on back
Shipping without blocking/reporting
Infinite scroll with a footer nobody can reach
Manipulative streak/notification mechanics

items.name: Travel / Booking
items.pattern: Search-first hero + results with real filters + a detail page + a booking flow
items.colorMood: Window seat at altitude — sky blue over sand with a coral CTA
items.typeMood: Clean and international; assume translation and long strings

decisionRules.then: the search form IS the hero — a destination photo above a buried search box is a decorative failure
show the total including fees from the first result; drip pricing is the category's defining dark pattern and is now illegal in several markets
dates, currency, and long translated strings will all break your layout — design for de-DE and ja-JP, not just en-US
state it at the point of decision, in body text, not in the confirmation email

antiPatterns: Fees revealed only at the last step
'2 people are looking at this right now' fabricated urgency
A hero photo where the search box should be
Date pickers that assume US format

items.name: Real Estate / Property
items.pattern: Search + map/list results + a photo-heavy listing page + enquiry CTA
items.colorMood: Old money without the crest — sage, limestone and brass
items.typeMood: Quietly premium; the property photography carries it

decisionRules.then: photos, price, location and size answer 90% of the question — everything else is secondary. Get those four on the card
sync it with the list and keep both keyboard-operable; a map-only interface excludes screen-reader users from the entire product
no urgency mechanics — they read as manipulative on the largest purchase of someone's life

antiPatterns: Listings with no price
Map-only browsing with no accessible list
Watermarked, low-resolution photos
Contact-gating the address

items.name: Automotive
items.pattern: Cinematic vehicle hero + specs + configurator + dealer/buy CTA
items.colorMood: Machined gunmetal with a brake-light red — engineered
items.typeMood: Technical and precise; specs are a feature
effects: spec tables that are actually readable

decisionRules.then: keep the running price visible at every step — a configurator that reveals the total at the end feels like a trap
real units and a comparison; a spec sheet nobody can compare against a rival is decoration
give it a static fallback and a real loading budget — it is usually the heaviest thing on the site

antiPatterns: A 40MB hero video
A configurator that hides the total until the end
Specs as an image
Financing terms in the footer

items.name: Legal / Professional Services
items.pattern: Credibility hero + practice areas + attorney bios + case results + consultation CTA
items.colorMood: Leather-bound and unbothered — oxblood on cream with brass
items.typeMood: Serious and traditional; a serif earns trust in this category
effects: essentially none — gravitas comes from restraint

decisionRules.then: they are frightened and in a hurry — the path to 'talk to a human' must be one tap from anywhere, and the copy must be plain English, not legalese
the jurisdiction's bar rules apply — required disclaimers are body text near the claim, not a footer afterthought
real photos and real credentials; this is a pure trust purchase

antiPatterns: Stock photos of gavels and scales
Legalese in the marketing copy
Missing required advertising disclaimers
A contact form as the only route to a human

items.name: Nonprofit / Charity
items.pattern: Story-led hero + the impact + where the money goes + donate CTA everywhere
items.colorMood: Hopeful and human — a living green with a coral for urgency
items.typeMood: Warm and human; a person tells this story, not a brand
effects: a progress bar toward a real goal
a donate button that is always reachable

decisionRules.then: show where it goes with a specific number — '£25 buys a week of meals' outperforms every abstract mission statement ever written
make it 2 steps and take Apple/Google Pay; every extra field measurably costs donations
dignity and consent first — no poverty-porn imagery, ever. It is both unethical and, with modern donors, ineffective
make cancellation as easy as signup; a charity that traps donors loses the next one too

antiPatterns: Poverty-porn imagery
A donate flow with 8 fields
Abstract mission copy with no concrete impact number
Hard-to-cancel recurring donations

items.name: Government / Civic
items.pattern: Task-first hero (what do you need to do?) + services + forms + contact
items.colorMood: Plain-spoken public service — federal navy and generous neutrals
items.typeMood: Maximum plainness; this must work for literally everyone
effects: none — this is infrastructure, not a brand exercise

decisionRules.then: accessibility is a legal requirement, not a priority band — WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor and the audit is real (Section 508, EN 301 549, the EAA)
organize by task, never by department — the org chart is your problem, not the citizen's. This is the category's single biggest failure
assume old devices, slow connections, screen readers and low digital literacy — this audience cannot opt out and go elsewhere
one question per page beats a wall of fields; the GOV.UK pattern exists because it was tested on everyone

antiPatterns: Navigation organized by department
A PDF as the only way to complete a task
Any accessibility gap — it is a legal exposure here
A JS-only interface with no fallback

items.name: Logistics / Supply Chain
items.pattern: Ops dashboard + tracking + exceptions queue + a scannable table
items.colorMood: Hi-vis on steel — warehouse amber against industrial grey
items.typeMood: Legible at a glance from a metre away, on a cheap screen

decisionRules.then: 56px targets, maximum contrast, and no hover anything — gloves, glare and a cracked screen are the actual design constraints. Test it outdoors at noon
the exception queue IS the product; nobody looks at the 98% that worked. Design for the failure case first
colour + icon + text, always — a colour-blind dispatcher misrouting freight is a real cost
the scan target is the whole screen, not a small box

antiPatterns: Hover-dependent controls on a touch device
Low contrast in a high-glare environment
Status by colour alone
Burying exceptions below the happy path

items.name: HR / People / Recruiting
items.pattern: Hero + the people problem it solves + the flow + integrations + demo CTA
items.colorMood: Warm plum with a teal that keeps it professional — softer than enterprise, still credible
items.typeMood: Human and approachable; this product is about people

decisionRules.then: the applicant is a user with no loyalty and no patience — a 40-field application after a CV upload is why your funnel leaks. Parse the CV or don't ask
it is sensitive PII; no third-party analytics on those pages, and be explicit about who can see what
say so plainly — candidates have a right to know, and increasingly a legal one (NYC LL144, the EU AI Act)
show progress and let people save and resume; day one is stressful enough

antiPatterns: Re-typing a CV that was just uploaded
A candidate portal that never says what happened
Undisclosed algorithmic screening
Ghosting built into the product's default state

items.name: Marketplace / Two-sided
items.pattern: Search + listings + a seller profile + reviews + a transaction flow
items.colorMood: Deep teal for the platform, a warm accent for the transaction — the platform recedes, the listings pop
items.typeMood: Neutral by design; the sellers bring the personality

decisionRules.then: you have two products with opposite needs — the buyer wants a filter, the seller wants a dashboard. One homepage cannot serve both; route them at the door
reviews, verification and dispute routes are the product, not features. The marketplace sells trust; the listings are just inventory
design the empty state as the primary state — a marketplace with 6 listings must not look like a marketplace with 6 listings
state it plainly to both sides; hidden take-rates are how marketplaces get disintermediated

antiPatterns: One homepage trying to serve buyers and sellers
Fake review counts
An empty state that exposes the cold-start problem
Hidden fees revealed at checkout

items.name: Dating / Relationships
items.pattern: Profile-first + discovery + matching + chat + safety centre
items.colorMood: Flushed but not tacky — rose and peach with a violet undertone
items.typeMood: Warm and personable; large enough to read one-handed on a couch

decisionRules.then: safety is the core flow: block, report, photo verification, and a visible route to help. Ship them with v1 — this is the one category where a UX gap becomes a physical-safety incident
never expose precise location; distance bands only. Trilateration from an exact distance is a documented real-world attack on this category
an undo, always — an accidental swipe is irreversible loss in a product built on chance
don't sell out of a problem you created; paywalling replies to a message someone already received is extortion-shaped

antiPatterns: Precise distance exposure
No undo on a swipe
Safety tools buried in settings
Paywalling a received message

items.name: Sports / Live Scores
items.pattern: Live scores + fixtures + standings + team pages + news
items.colorMood: Kickoff — scarlet on midnight with a floodlight yellow
items.typeMood: Condensed and bold; a score must be readable from across a room

decisionRules.then: the score is the largest thing on the screen and updates without a refresh — announce updates via aria-live or screen-reader users get a silent page
they want one number in under two seconds; every interstitial between them and the score is a lost user
offer a spoiler-free mode — a highlights page that shows the score above the video is a product that hates its users

antiPatterns: The score below an ad
Live updates that screen readers never hear
Scores spoiled above the highlights video
An interstitial before a two-second check

items.name: Photography / Visual
items.pattern: Full-bleed gallery + series/collections + about + licensing or booking
items.colorMood: Safelight — neutral greys calibrated not to lie about a photograph
items.typeMood: Nearly invisible; the interface must not tint the work

decisionRules.then: the UI must be chromatically neutral — a coloured background shifts the perceived colour of every photo on it. This is why galleries are grey
AVIF plus responsive srcset, and a real LCP budget — photographers ship the slowest sites on the web and it costs them work
make the terms clear and the enquiry trivial; right-click blocking is theatre that only annoys clients

antiPatterns: A coloured or branded background behind the photographs
Right-click disabling
12MB JPEGs
A watermark across the middle of the frame

items.name: Minimal / Personal Site
items.pattern: A short intro + links + writing + contact. That's it.
items.colorMood: Nothing but greys and one blue that appears only when you can click it
items.typeMood: One typeface, three sizes, done well
effects: none — restraint is the entire aesthetic

decisionRules.then: minimal means fewer elements, not smaller and greyer ones. Thin grey text on white is not minimalism, it is an accessibility failure wearing minimalism's clothes
ship it — a plain page that exists beats a beautiful one that never launches

antiPatterns: #999 body text mistaken for taste
A loading animation on a 40KB page
So minimal that the navigation is a mystery

items.name: Brutalist / Experimental
items.pattern: Deliberately broken conventions — but one clear path through
items.colorMood: Unfinished on purpose — raw concrete, hard black rules and a single alarm colour
items.typeMood: System fonts, enormous, unapologetic

decisionRules.then: break the aesthetic, never the access — brutalism is famously high-contrast and semantic, which is exactly why it works. Unusable is not a style, it is a bug with a manifesto
still ship keyboard navigation and focus states; the people who most appreciate this aesthetic will be the first to notice you skipped them

antiPatterns: Illegibility defended as intent
Removed focus states
A layout that traps a keyboard user
Brutalism as a costume on a bank

items.name: Terminal / CLI Tool
items.pattern: Install command + an asciinema demo + flags reference + GitHub
items.colorMood: A CRT that never got switched off — phosphor green on near-black
items.typeMood: Mono throughout; the aesthetic is the product's own output
effects: a real terminal recording, not a fake typing animation

decisionRules.then: use a real asciinema recording — a faked typing animation is instantly obvious to this audience and reads as a lie about the product
check the contrast for real; classic terminal green on black often lands near 3:1 and the aesthetic is not worth the readability
a searchable reference beats a prose tour — nobody reads a CLI site top to bottom

antiPatterns: A fake typing animation
Green on black at 2.5:1
Screenshots of terminal output instead of copyable text
A blinking cursor next to body copy

items.name: Documentation Site
items.pattern: Persistent sidebar + the content column + an on-page table of contents + search
items.colorMood: Quiet and neutral — the code blocks are the only colour
items.typeMood: A real reading size for prose, mono for anything executable
effects: copy button on every code block

decisionRules.then: search is the primary navigation — people arrive from Google mid-task, land deep, and need to know where they are. Breadcrumbs and a visible sidebar position are not decoration
the version switcher is prominent and the URL carries the version — docs showing v3 to someone on v2 is worse than no docs
copyable, complete, and actually runnable; a snippet with three elided imports wastes more time than it saves

antiPatterns: A docs site with no search
Truncated examples with '...'
No indication of which version is being read
Prose where a table belongs

items.name: Sustainability / Organic
items.pattern: Story hero + the practice + proof/certification + product or action CTA
items.colorMood: Clay, moss and oat — pigments that look mixed rather than picked
items.typeMood: Warm and grounded; a slab serif reads as honest here

decisionRules.then: cite the certification or the number — unsubstantiated green claims are now regulated (the EU Green Claims Directive) and readers are primed to disbelieve them
the site should be light — a 5MB page about carbon footprint is an own goal that reviewers will notice

antiPatterns: Green colour as the entire sustainability claim
Vague 'eco-friendly' with no substantiation
A heavy, energy-hungry site about energy

items.name: Accessibility-first Product
items.pattern: Plain hero + the tasks + settings that genuinely adapt the interface
items.colorMood: Every pair pushed past AA and most of the way to AAA
items.typeMood: Chosen for legibility above all — Atkinson Hyperlegible exists for exactly this
effects: focus states that are impossible to miss

decisionRules.then: AAA where it is achievable, and test with real assistive tech — shipping an a11y product that fails NVDA is the most embarrassing possible outcome
they must actually change the product, not just a font size — respect prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast and forced-colors natively first
the keyboard path is the primary path, not the fallback

antiPatterns: An accessibility overlay widget — they are widely condemned by disabled users and invite litigation
Claiming compliance without an audit
A settings panel that is itself inaccessible
